transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-05
- Start: 16:30 PST
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Location: Zoom
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Iris Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Emberbyte Head of Security), Tom Brice (Emberbyte Platform), Priya Nair (CTO), Evan Liu (SRE)

Summary: quick intros, then a deep security intake. Customer concerned about PII handling, retention windows, and ability to run private in a VPC with customer KMS/HSM. Redwood team walked through hosted/dedicated/private differences and compliance artifacts to follow up.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:04 Priya Nair: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:12 Maya Chen: cool, quick intros then we can jump to high level ask — we're here to understand your security and deployment constraints, especially around keys, auditability, and data residency.
00:25 Leah Park: great, i'm Leah, head of security at Emberbyte. We're evaluating for inference on sensitive patient-derived notes, so SOC two and encryption are musts.
00:36 Tom Brice: Tom here, we run their infra on AWS, mainly us-east-1, we want to avoid egress if possible.
00:45 Daniel Ruiz: thanks, Tom. To set expectations: Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private modes — hosted is quickest, dedicated is reserved capacity with some isolation, private gives you control over data plane and VPC. We'll go through each in the context of your requirements.
00:57 Evan Liu: question already, in private does the control plane still talk to Redwood's cloud? We need to know what crosses public internet.
01:05 Iris Patel: short answer: there's an optional private control plane for enterprise where the management plane can be customer-hosted, and data plane can be fully isolated in customer VPC. we'll share network diagrams.
01:18 Leah Park: ok good, because our compliance team will balk at any unmanaged egress. We also require KMS with customer key rotation policies.
01:28 Daniel Ruiz: we support customer-managed KMS integrations for cloud providers; for on-prem HSM we can integrate via KMIP or bring-your-own-HSM patterns but that'll be more involved — typically for Redwood Private.
01:45 Priya Nair: does that mean hosted is out for us? we were hoping to move faster but security might block that.
01:53 Maya Chen: hosted might be fine if you don't need customer-managed keys and are ok with our SOC two controls and contractual terms. but you said patient-derived notes — that usually triggers Private or Dedicated with strict KMS.
02:10 Leah Park: also need to confirm SOC two recency, like which date and scope, and any ISO 27001 if available.
02:18 Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted and dedicated control planes — we'll attach the report. We also have ISO 27001 certification in progress across our control plane services — i'll include timelines.
02:33 Tom Brice: about audit logs — do you provide raw event logs? we want to ship them to our S3 and feed them into SIEM.
02:40 Daniel Ruiz: yes, audit events can be exported to customer sinks (S3, CloudWatch, Splunk) for private and dedicated; hosted has export capabilities too but with longer retention options. logs include per-request metadata, model id, route, token usage, and who invoked.
02:58 Leah Park: is that redaction friendly? we won't want raw prompt text to land in long-lived storage.
03:06 Iris Patel: we do configurable masking and policy-based redaction for prompts; for private deployments you can enforce prompt truncation and retention via config. hosted defaults to retention X (we'll share exact numbers) but enterprise customers can set shorter retention.
03:25 Evan Liu: how about RBAC? can we have teams with route-level permissions and scoped API keys?
03:33 Daniel Ruiz: yes, RBAC is role-based, supports SSO via SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and token scoping per route or model. there are caveats with some older SDKs, but modern SDKs honor route-level tokens.
03:51 Leah Park: SAML sounds good; does Redwood support IdP-initiated flows and SCIM for user provisioning?
03:58 Maya Chen: both supported. SCIM can auto-provision groups and map to RBAC roles. we'll share a sample SAML metadata file.
04:10 Priya Nair: in terms of encryption in transit, TLS 1.2/1.3? mutual TLS for peering?
04:16 Daniel Ruiz: we support TLS 1.2+ and can configure mTLS for VPC peering and internal links in private deployments.
04:28 Tom Brice: network diagram request — we need to know ports, egress flows, and what controls we need on our side.
04:35 Iris Patel: noted, Daniel will prepare a diagram and a minimal firewall/route table list.
04:40 Leah Park: about data residency — will my data ever leave us-east-1?
04:45 Maya Chen: for private deployments, data stays in your VPC/region. for hosted we have region options but there are some control plane interactions possibly cross-region; we'll detail that.
04:56 Evan Liu: ok, some specifics on retention policy: we have to retain logs for 7 years for some audit trails, but for prompts containing PHI we cannot retain beyond 30 days. can Redwood support both simultaneously?
05:10 Daniel Ruiz: you can configure two tiers: operational audit logs (7 years) and prompt/text payload retention (configurable, can be 0-90 days). for hosted we'd need policy addendum; private gives full control.
05:30 Leah Park: interesting — what about data deletion / right-to-be-forgotten requests?
05:36 Iris Patel: we have data-deletion APIs and certs for deletion requests; in private it's straightforward since data is in your storage. for hosted we provide deletion windows and audit trail for deletions.
05:48 Priya Nair: any concerns around model caching or KV cache keeping prompt snippets?
05:55 Daniel Ruiz: KV cache exists to speed up generation; for enterprise we can disable cross-request caching of sensitive keys and also encrypt caches at rest with customer keys in private deployments.
06:08 Tom Brice: does Redwood store embeddings? we plan to compute embeddings for retrieval, those might be derived from PHI.
06:16 Maya Chen: embeddings can be routed to your own vector DB in private mode; hosted has an embedding store option but enterprise customers often choose to push embeddings to their own store.
06:30 Leah Park: let's talk about threat model — what about insider risk at Redwood and logs of admin access?
06:36 Iris Patel: admin access is audited; we have breakglass flows, session recording, and privileged access reviews. SOC2 covers many of those controls. we'll provide a description of our privileged access process.
06:50 Evan Liu: on the KMS integration — we use AWS KMS with custom key policies, can Redwood do envelope encryption with our CMKs?
06:58 Daniel Ruiz: yes — envelope encryption with your CMK is standard for cloud KMS. for HSM we integrate via KMIP but there is some engineering lead time.
07:12 Leah Park: if we opt for Redwood Private in our VPC, does Redwood need any persistent creds? we prefer short-lived tokens.
07:20 Maya Chen: recommended pattern is ephemeral role-based credentials and mutual TLS between our runtime and your VPC. we can also use AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering depending on topology.
07:33 Tom Brice: curious about billing and data separation — if we have dedicated capacity, are logs and metrics logically separated from other customers?
07:40 Daniel Ruiz: dedicated gives resource isolation at the GPU level and logical separation in logs/metrics; private gives full tenancy separation.
07:50 Priya Nair: latency — we have 50ms tail SLOs for some real-time features; can Redwood meet that in private or dedicated?
07:59 Daniel Ruiz: we tune runtime for low-latency; dedicated can meet strict SLOs with reserved pools. private latency depends on your infra; we can run benchmarks during pilot.
08:12 Leah Park: how do you do key rotation without downtime?
08:18 Iris Patel: we support key rotation workflows with seamless re-encryption for new tokens, and can do rolling rekeys for minimal impact. we'll provide the rotation doc.
08:32 Evan Liu: if we need to prove chain of custody for certain requests, can logs include pre/post hashed values so we can verify integrity without exposing plaintext?
08:40 Daniel Ruiz: yes, we can log hashed request ids and cryptographic checksums and export them to your SIEM for chain-of-custody proofs.
08:54 Maya Chen: switching gears — any red flags from your side? what's a blocker vs wishlist?
09:00 Leah Park: blocker is any uncontrolled KMS or storage of PHI outside our control. wishlist includes per-route quota controls and more granular RBAC.
09:12 Tom Brice: we also want CI/CD friendly deploys — terraform modules or helm charts if private.
09:18 Iris Patel: we have terraform modules for private deployments and a helm chart for on-prem runtime. will include links.
09:28 Priya Nair: ok, maybe to summarize: leaning private but want to validate complexity and timelines.
09:35 Maya Chen: perfect — we'll send SOC2, ISO timeline, network diagram, KMS integration patterns, and pilot plan. recommended next meeting: pilot kickoff.
09:46 Leah Park: can we get a sample contract clause for data residency and breach notification windows?
09:52 Maya Chen: yes i'll loop in legal and share a standard addendum.
10:00 Tom Brice: one more technical — for SCIM mapping, can groups map to route-level roles?
10:07 Daniel Ruiz: yeah SCIM groups map to RBAC roles and you can scope to models/routes; we have examples.
10:15 Evan Liu: any limits on API key scoping? like per-model token quotas?
10:21 Iris Patel: tokens can be scoped by route, model, and quota; quotas are enforced at gateway.
10:28 Leah Park: ok thanks — feel like we're getting a clearer picture.
10:34 Maya Chen: awesome. quick housekeeping: i'll email the artifacts and propose pilot dates.
10:40 Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
10:44 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up.
10:48 call end

Notes on transcription: there are occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache sometimes listed as K V cache, KMIP spelled out), proper nouns may be imperfect. Links mentioned: SOC2_report.pdf (will be attached), private-deploy-network-diagram.png, scim-saml-sample-metadata.xml, terraform-module-README.md.
